Not everyone knows this (and I won’t pretend I did), but Apple has published extremely detailed dimensional drawings of dozens of devices on its website to help accessory manufacturers design their products. Here are the details.

Apple Hardware, in Exhaustive Detail

For nearly three decades, Jason Kottke has been one of my main sources for discovering interesting things on the internet (and beyond), and without him I would certainly have missed out on a lot of treasures.

A few days ago, he posted a piece linking to the “Dimensional Drawings” section of the “Accessories” area on Apple’s developer site.

In short, it’s a database containing highly detailed technical drawings of a total of 96 current products, including the brand-new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and the AirPods 5.

The list also includes products such as the MacBook Neo and Siri Remote, as well as accessories like the AirTag, AirPods charging case, and even the ZEISS optical lens accessories for Apple Vision Pro.

Each document contains precise measurements ranging from the overall dimensions and curves of the device down to buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers, and connectors, along with detailed “keep-out” markings and instructions indicating where certain materials should not be placed.

Although these documents are primarily intended for accessory makers, anyone with even a passing interest in hardware or industrial design—or simply someone who appreciates the meticulousness of Apple products—will find them fascinating to browse.

To view Apple’s dimensional drawings, follow this link. And if you don’t already follow kottke.org, be sure to do so right away.

Notable Products on Amazon

  • Apple Watch Series 12
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods 5
  • AirTag (2nd Generation) — 4-Pack
  • MacBook Neo
